name: Burmese
variant: Colloquial (spoken) Burmese of Yangon and Mandalay, the everyday register with တယ်, မယ်, လား, လဲ and ဘူး, not the formal literary register (သည်, မည်, ၏) used in books and news; written in Burmese script, with a romanisation shown under the script as a reading aid in the first lessons
variant_ko: 양곤·만달레이의 구어체 미얀마어: 책과 뉴스에 쓰는 격식 문어체(သည်, မည်, ၏)가 아니라 တယ်, မယ်, လား, လဲ, ဘူး를 쓰는 일상 구어체입니다. 미얀마 문자로 쓰고, 처음 몇 과에서는 읽기를 돕기 위해 문자 아래에 로마자 표기를 보여 줍니다
script: Burmese (Myanmar) script, left to right: 33 consonant letters, vowel signs written before, after, above and below the consonant, tone marks ့ and း, the killer stroke ် (asat), medials ျ ြ ွ ှ and stacked consonants; Burmese digits ၀–၉; no spaces between words
basis: Topic order of San San Hnin Tun with Patrick McCormick, Colloquial Burmese: The Complete Course for Beginners (Routledge, 2014): a preliminary unit on greetings, script and numbers, then meeting people, new in town, weather, family and friends, lost in the street, food and drink, likes and wishes, abilities, needs, being considerate in public, plans and travel, time, past experiences, getting sick and where you are
basis_ko: San San Hnin Tun·Patrick McCormick, Colloquial Burmese (Routledge, 2014)의 주제 순서: 인사·문자·숫자의 예비 단원 다음에 처음 만나기, 새 동네, 날씨, 가족과 친구, 길 잃기, 음식과 음료, 좋아함과 바람, 능력, 필요, 공공장소 예절, 계획과 여행, 시간, 과거 경험, 아플 때, 있는 곳 말하기
src: Routledge product page for San San Hnin Tun and Patrick McCormick, Colloquial Burmese: The Complete Course for Beginners (ISBN 9781138958142), read through a fetch summary on 2026-11-24: full table of contents (Preliminary unit: greetings, Burmese script and numbers; units 1-15: A curious foreigner, New in town, Talking about weather, Family and friends, Lost in the street, Food and drinks, Likes and dislikes, wishes and desires, Abilities and talents, Getting thirsty and other needs, Being considerate in public spaces, Plans for the weekend and travel plans, Talking about time, Past experiences, Getting sick, Talking about where you are; five reviews) and the description. The page does not say which romanisation or register the book uses; the book itself was not opened
note: The topic order follows the Routledge contents, with these changes: being at a place (unit 15, Talking about where you are) is moved into the first-sentences stage because the place words မှာ / ကို / က are needed early; weather (unit 3), needs (unit 9), getting sick (unit 14) and the reviews are left out; ability is taught with must in one lesson; requests are taught with being considerate (unit 10) and before plans (unit 11), and time (unit 12) after plans, as in the book. The split of the script into four lessons, the grammar point chosen for each topic, every Burmese form in the titles and the Korean titles are my own (common course practice and own knowledge). Romanisation: the page does not say what the book uses, so the system is still to be chosen; John Okell's romanisation (from his Burmese course books) and the Myanmar Language Commission transcription are the usual candidates (own knowledge, not checked this session). Pronouns ကျွန်တော် / ကျွန်မ differ by the speaker's sex and must be taught both ways. Writers must check every Burmese form with a first-language speaker.
hardest: Tones and phonation: low, high, creaky and stopped syllables (ခါ, ခါး, ခ, ခတ်)
A round script with vowel signs on every side of the consonant, stacked letters and no spaces between words
Two registers: colloquial endings (တယ်, မယ်) against literary ones (သည်, မည်) that learners see in writing
Classifiers after numbers (လူ နှစ်ယောက်) and pronouns that change with the speaker's sex

items: my-tones
Tones: low, high, creaky and stopped syllables (ခါ, ခါး, ခ, ခတ်), with romanisation
성조: 낮은 소리, 높은 소리, 짧고 끊는 소리, 막힌 음절(ခါ, ခါး, ခ, ခတ်), 로마자 표기와 함께
my-consonants
The consonant letters: က ခ ဂ င, aspirated and plain sounds
자음 글자: က ခ ဂ င, 기식음과 평음
my-vowels
Vowel signs and tone marks: ာ ိ ီ ု ူ ေ ဲ, with ့ and း
모음 기호와 성조 표시: ာ ိ ီ ု ူ ေ ဲ, 그리고 ့와 း
my-finals
Finals and medials: the asat ် and ျ ြ ွ ှ
받침과 중간 자음: 아땃 ်, 그리고 ျ ြ ွ ှ
my-greetings
Greetings: မင်္ဂလာပါ, နေကောင်းလား?, ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်
인사: မင်္ဂလာပါ, နေကောင်းလား?, ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်
my-intro
Introducing yourself: ကျွန်တော့် / ကျွန်မ နာမည် … ပါ; နာမည် ဘယ်လို ခေါ်လဲ?
자기소개: ကျွန်တော့် / ကျွန်မ နာမည် … ပါ; နာမည် ဘယ်လို ခေါ်လဲ?
my-pronouns
Pronouns: ကျွန်တော် (men), ကျွန်မ (women), ခင်ဗျား / ရှင်, သူ
대명사: ကျွန်တော်(남성), ကျွန်မ(여성), ခင်ဗျား / ရှင်, သူ
my-noun-sentences
Noun sentences: ဒါ စာအုပ်ပါ; yes-no questions with လား
명사 문장: ဒါ စာအုပ်ပါ; လား로 묻는 예/아니요 질문
my-questions
Question words with လဲ: ဘာ, ဘယ်သူ, ဘယ်မှာ, ဘယ်တော့, ဘယ်လောက်
လဲ와 함께 쓰는 의문사: ဘာ, ဘယ်သူ, ဘယ်မှာ, ဘယ်တော့, ဘယ်လောက်
my-verbs
Verb sentences with တယ် (သွားတယ်, စားတယ်) and negation မ…ဘူး
တယ်로 끝나는 동사 문장(သွားတယ်, စားတယ်)과 မ…ဘူး 부정
my-numbers
Numbers and prices: တစ်, နှစ်, သုံး … ဆယ်; ကျပ်
숫자와 가격: တစ်, နှစ်, သုံး … ဆယ်; ကျပ်
my-classifiers
Classifiers: ယောက် (people), ခု (things), ကောင် (animals); လူ နှစ်ယောက်
분류사: ယောက်(사람), ခု(물건), ကောင်(동물); လူ နှစ်ယောက်
my-shi
There is and have: ရှိတယ် / မရှိဘူး; family (အမေ, အဖေ, အစ်ကို, ညီမ)
있다와 가지다: ရှိတယ် / မရှိဘူး; 가족(အမေ, အဖေ, အစ်ကို, ညီမ)
my-place
Place and movement: မှာ (at), ကို (to), က (from); ရန်ကုန်မှာ နေတယ်
장소와 이동: မှာ(~에), ကို(~로), က(~에서); ရန်ကုန်မှာ နေတယ်
my-directions
Directions and transport: ညာဘက်, ဘယ်ဘက်, တည့်တည့်; တက္ကစီ, ဘတ်စ်ကား
길 묻기와 교통: ညာဘက်, ဘယ်ဘက်, တည့်တည့်; တက္ကစီ, ဘတ်စ်ကား
my-food
Ordering food and drink: ထမင်း, လက်ဖက်ရည်, … ပေးပါ; ပိုက်ဆံ ရှင်းမယ်
음식과 음료 주문: ထမင်း, လက်ဖက်ရည်, … ပေးပါ; ပိုက်ဆံ ရှင်းမယ်
my-want
Wanting: ချင်တယ် (want to do), လိုချင်တယ် (want a thing)
원하기: ချင်တယ်(~하고 싶다), လိုချင်တယ်(~을 갖고 싶다)
my-like
Likes and dislikes: ကြိုက်တယ် / မကြိုက်ဘူး
좋아함과 싫어함: ကြိုက်တယ် / မကြိုက်ဘူး
my-can
Can and must: တတ်တယ် (know how), နိုင်တယ် (be able), ရမယ် (must)
할 수 있다와 해야 한다: တတ်တယ်(할 줄 안다), နိုင်တယ်(할 수 있다), ရမယ်(해야 한다)
my-requests
Polite requests and commands: ပါ, နော်; don't with မ…နဲ့
공손한 부탁과 명령: ပါ, နော်; 금지는 မ…နဲ့
my-future
Plans and the future with မယ်: သွားမယ်, မသွားဘူး
မယ်로 말하는 계획과 미래: သွားမယ်, မသွားဘူး
my-time
Time and days: ဘယ်နှစ်နာရီ ရှိပြီလဲ?, တနင်္လာ, မနက်ဖြန်
시간과 요일: ဘယ်နှစ်နာရီ ရှိပြီလဲ?, တနင်္လာ, မနက်ဖြန်
my-past
Past events and 'already': ခဲ့တယ်, ပြီ (စားပြီးပြီ)
과거의 일과 '벌써': ခဲ့တယ်, ပြီ (စားပြီးပြီ)
my-experience
Experience and joining sentences: ဖူးတယ် (have ever), ပြီးတော့, ဒါပေမဲ့
경험과 문장 잇기: ဖူးတယ်(~해 본 적 있다), ပြီးတော့, ဒါပေမဲ့
